backlogOrders.title: Backlog, orders and organic orders growth
backlogOrders.content:
Backlog is the dollar value of signed but not-yet-executed work; orders received is new business booked in the period; organic orders growth strips out FX and the Bosch R&LC divestiture to isolate underlying demand.

For Johnson Controls International plc: data-center/AI-infrastructure cooling demand pushed FY2026 backlog to $23.0bn (from $16.6bn in FY2025) on orders of roughly $29.7bn and organic orders growth of ~35%, giving multi-quarter revenue visibility well ahead of the P&L.

What to watch:

  • Whether backlog growth keeps outrunning revenue growth (building visibility) or starts converting (revenue catching up)
  • Orders growth decelerating from the ~35% organic pace, especially if data-center capex slows
  • Book-to-bill (orders vs. revenue) above 1x signals an expanding backlog

segmentRevenue.title: Segment revenue by region
segmentRevenue.content:
Revenue split across JCI's three Building Solutions segments: Americas, EMEA (incl. Latin America) and Asia Pacific.

For Johnson Controls International plc: Americas (~69% of segment revenue) is the data-center growth engine, with Q4 FY2026 organic growth of 14%; EMEA (~18%) has been held back by Middle East disruption (Q4 organic +3%); Asia Pacific (~12%) is growing (Q4 organic +13%) but off a small base.

What to watch:

  • Whether EMEA's softness is temporary (conflict-related) or a structural lag versus Americas
  • Asia Pacific's growth rate relative to its share of backlog -- it carries a larger share of backlog than of current revenue

organicGrowth.title: Organic sales growth
organicGrowth.content:
Organic growth is revenue growth excluding currency translation and the effect of acquisitions/divestitures (notably the August 2025 sale of the Residential & Light Commercial business to Bosch) -- the cleanest read on underlying demand.

For Johnson Controls International plc: organic growth accelerated from 6% in FY2025 to 8% in FY2026, management's clearest evidence that data-center-driven orders and backlog are starting to show up in reported sales. Only reported annually, hence no interim toggle here.

What to watch:

  • Whether the acceleration continues as the much larger FY2026 backlog converts to revenue
  • Divergence between organic growth and reported revenue growth (FX, portfolio changes)

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Johnson Controls International plc: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Johnson Controls International plc: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Johnson Controls International plc: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Johnson Controls International plc: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Johnson Controls International plc: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Johnson Controls International plc: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Johnson Controls International plc: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Johnson Controls International plc: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Johnson Controls International plc: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Johnson Controls International plc: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
